description: Gold-standard point-in-time statutory retrieval and temporal resolution evaluation suite comprising 10 multi-era Indian legal scenarios.

test_cases.title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property Across Criminal Law Transition

expected_resolution.constitutional_basis: Constitution of India, Article 20(1) (Protection against ex post facto criminal laws)
expected_resolution.expected_substantive_text_fragment: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
expected_resolution.expected_procedural_note: Trial and investigation proceed under BNSS 2023 because no investigation/inquiry/trial was pending prior to 01.07.2024

expected_resolution.expected_substantive_text_fragment: Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both
expected_resolution.expected_procedural_note: Governed exclusively by BNS 2023 substantively and BNSS 2023 procedurally

test_cases.title: Electronic Record Admissibility Certificate Era Comparison

post_transition.condition: Section 63 certificate requirement including Schedule format

test_cases.title: Specific Relief Act Section 10 Discretionary vs Mandatory Regime

pre_amendment.operative_phrase: the specific performance of any contract may, in the discretion of the court, be enforced

post_amendment.operative_phrase: The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16

test_cases.title: Arbitration and Conciliation Section 34 Challenge Commencement Boundary

pre_2015_commenced.applicability: Section 26 of 2015 Amendment Act specifies amendment does not apply unless parties agree
pre_2015_commenced.landmark_precedent: BCCI v. Kochi Cricket Pvt. Ltd. (2018) 6 SCC 287

post_2015_commenced.applicability: 2015 Amendment Act applies including Section 34(2A) patent illegality restriction

test_cases.title: Data Breach Compensation and Phased Commencement of DPDP Act 2023

expected_resolution.status_determination: IT Act Section 43A remains active and enforceable because DPDP Act Section 44 has not been notified under Section 1(2)

era_1.title: Consumer Protection Act, 1986
era_1.determination: Filed under CPA 1986, jurisdiction governed by value of goods/services and compensation claimed

era_2.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
era_2.district_commission_limit: INR 1 Crore (later adjusted to 50 Lakhs via 2021 Rules)
era_2.determination: Filed under CPA 2019, pending proceedings not transferred unless covered by rules (Neena Aneja v. New India Assurance)

test_cases.title: Negotiable Instruments Act Section 143A Interim Compensation Prospectivity

pre_amendment_complaints.statutory_rule: Section 143A introduced by Act 20 of 2018 is prospective and cannot be applied to complaints filed prior to 01.09.2018 (G.J. Raja v. Tejraj Sharma, (2019) 19 SCC 469)

post_amendment_complaints.statutory_rule: Court trying Section 138 offense may order interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount

test_cases.title: Unlawful Assembly and Rioting with Pre-July Incident and Post-July Trial

substantive_provisions.concept: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offense committed in prosecution of common object

procedural_provisions.concept: Investigation and trial procedure governed by BNSS 2023 under s.531(2)(a)

expected_resolution.substantive_bns_inapplicability: BNS 2023 Section 189/190 cannot be retrospectively applied to an incident occurring in February 2024

test_cases.title: Electronic Signature Validity and Recognition Under Information Technology Act

expected_resolution.validity: Active and in force throughout the interval [2009-10-27, null)
